title: firebase.json is not valid JSON
msg: firebase.json does not parse as JSON, so the CLI cannot read it and nothing below could be checked. Fix the syntax first.
fix: Run `firebase deploy --only hosting --dry-run` and fix the reported position.

title: public root is the whole repository
msg: hosting.public points at the repository root, so every file the ignore list misses ships to the public CDN — including .git history, README drafts and local scripts.
fix: Point hosting.public at your build output directory (dist, build, public).

title: no public directory declared
msg: This hosting block declares neither `public` nor `source`, so `firebase deploy` will refuse the target or fall back to a directory you did not choose.
fix: Add "public": "<your build output>" to the hosting block.

title: no ignore list — defaults only
msg: With no ignore list Firebase applies its three defaults (firebase.json, **/.*, **/node_modules/**). Source maps, service-account JSON and backup files inside the public directory are still uploaded.
fix: Add an explicit ignore array that repeats the three defaults and adds **/*.map and key files.

title: ignore list drops the dotfile default
msg: Supplying hosting.ignore REPLACES Firebase's defaults, and this list has no **/.* entry. Every dotfile under the public root — .env, .env.production, .npmrc, .git — is uploaded and served.
fix: Add "**/.*" back to the ignore array.

title: .env files are not excluded
msg: Nothing in the ignore list excludes .env files, so a .env or .env.production sitting in the build output is fetchable at https://<site>/.env by anyone who guesses the path.

title: source maps ship to production
msg: No ignore entry matches *.map, so the bundler's .map files publish next to the minified code and hand any visitor your unminified source, comments and internal paths.
fix: Add "**/*.map" to hosting.ignore, or turn sourcemaps off in the production build.

title: admin key files are not excluded
msg: No ignore entry matches a service-account key (serviceAccount*.json, *adminsdk*.json, *.pem). One of those left in the build folder is a full Firebase Admin credential served over HTTPS.

title: node_modules is not fully excluded
msg: The ignore list has no "**/node_modules/**" entry, so nested dependency folders under the public root are uploaded file by file — a slow deploy that also publishes package sources.

title: firebase.json itself is not ignored
msg: "firebase.json" is a Firebase default that your custom ignore list dropped, so this config — target names, rewrite map, header policy — is served from your own domain.

title: no response headers configured
msg: This hosting block sets no headers at all, so the site answers with Firebase defaults: no Content-Security-Policy, no HSTS, no nosniff and no framing rule.
fix: Add a headers entry with source "**" and the four baseline security headers.

title: no Content-Security-Policy header
msg: No headers rule sets Content-Security-Policy, so any injected or third-party script on the page runs with full privileges and can read the signed-in user's Firebase ID token.
fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header on the "**" source, starting from default-src 'self'.

title: no Strict-Transport-Security header
msg: Without Strict-Transport-Security a first visit over http:// can be intercepted before the redirect to https:// completes.

title: no X-Content-Type-Options header
msg: Without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a file a user uploaded and you serve back can be sniffed into an executable content type by the browser.

title: page can be framed by any site
msg: Neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive is set, so your signed-in app can be loaded in an invisible iframe on someone else's domain.
fix: Add "X-Frame-Options": "DENY" or frame-ancestors 'none' in the CSP.

title: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is *
msg: A headers rule returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on a broad source, so every other origin can read the responses this site serves, including any JSON the app fetches from its own path.
fix: Scope the header to the exact asset paths that need it, or name the allowed origin.

title: HTML cached long-term
msg: An HTML source is served with a long max-age, so browsers and the CDN keep serving the previous index.html after a deploy and users load old asset hashes that no longer exist.
fix: Serve HTML with "Cache-Control": "max-age=0, must-revalidate" and keep long caching for hashed assets only.
